doc.title: Jason Palmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 2, 2025

title: Freddie Hubbard on Blue Note sessions recorded after all-night gigs
summary: Palmer recalls Hubbard saying Blue Note dates followed late gigs and breakfast, then Rudy Van Gelder's studio; Rowe adds a Joe Williams story.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Right? Yeah. Either coming home from a gig or, you know, if you look at those like really consequential Blue Note records, a lot of those were started, you know, they started recording at that time. And you know I met Fred — well I’ll just start off with a story. I met Freddie Hubbard back in the late ‘90s and he told me a lot of those records that they made, you know, were recorded in the morning and so there were times when they would play a gig and they’d play several sets and it’d end at 3, 4, 5 in the morning. They’d go have breakfast and then go to Rudy VanGelder’s place. So yeah.

I wonder if that’s, you know, adrenaline kicks in. Coffee and whatever else sometimes resulted in terrific records. I remember Joe Williams had the same story about when he did the Thad Jones-Mel Lewis recording and no one had gone to bed yet.
